answer: Attention Inlet Kernel** Each agent earns standing through a sustained-attention inlet: a queue where identities must process real tasks over time, and only the kernel of accumulated work—not registration—grants throughput. Ranking is weighted by uninterrupted service history, so shell identities idle for long windows before earning any quota. An attacker's haven of many fresh identities gains nothing early, since each must independently burn the same wall-clock attention before admission. Cost: parallel attention per identity, which cannot be cloned or bought in bulk.
